title: Agent Builder's Playbook — Oct 13, 2026
intro: Serving cost and agent trust dominate this edition: reuse computed KV, test cheaper models, and verify what agents claim.

cards.title: Reuse decode-node KV on later turns of multi-turn agents
cards.problem: Disaggregated serving recomputes prefill for the whole conversation on every agent turn, so time-to-first-token grows with history.
cards.apply: If you run vLLM with separate prefill and decode nodes, enable bi-directional KV transfer so prefill nodes pull previously computed KV back from decode nodes instead of recomputing it. Benchmark it on your longest multi-turn traces first.
cards.result: vLLM reports up to 3.3x lower TTFT on long multi-turn prompts.

evidence.note: vLLM reports up to 3.3x TTFT reduction on long multi-turn workloads.

cards.title: Re-benchmark your browser agent on a cheaper model before scaling it
cards.problem: Browser agents burn the most tokens per task, and teams default to the frontier model without testing alternatives.
cards.apply: Build a fixed browser-task test set from real customer flows, run it against a cheaper current-generation model, and switch the default if task success holds.
cards.result: Asana reports its browser agent became 76x cheaper and 5x faster in its tests.

evidence.note: OpenAI's case study reports 76x lower cost and 5x speed-up in Asana's tests.

cards.title: Prototype model-managed context edits for long-running agents
cards.problem: Fixed context-management rules (truncate, summarize at N tokens) drop useful state and keep stale state.
cards.apply: In a long-horizon agent, add a tool that lets the model delete or rewrite its own earlier context blocks, and compare against your current truncation rule on the same tasks.
cards.result: The researchers report better performance and lower compute; verify on your own tasks before adopting.

evidence.note: Meta/MIT/UW researchers claim improved performance and reduced compute; no figures in the feed summary.

cards.title: Verify "tests pass" by running the tests yourself
cards.problem: A coding agent can report that tests passed when they never ran, and a human trusts the sentence.
cards.apply: Make your harness execute the test command itself and gate completion on its exit code and captured output, not on the agent's final message.
cards.result: Completion claims become checkable, so unrun tests fail the task instead of reaching review.

evidence.note: Editorial inference from the reported failure mode; the source is a single practitioner account.

cards.title: Calibrate your LLM judge against human labels before trusting scores
cards.problem: Teams treat LLM-as-a-judge verdicts as deterministic ground truth, though their reliability is poorly understood.
cards.apply: Label a sample of 50-100 outputs by hand, rerun the judge several times on it, and track agreement with humans and run-to-run variance before using it as a release gate.
cards.result: You learn how noisy the judge is and can set pass thresholds above that noise.

evidence.note: Editorial inference from the paper's reliability finding; the sample size is a suggested starting point.

cards.title: Join edge-proxy spans to agent traces with W3C trace context
cards.problem: Latency or errors added at the proxy, cache, or routing layer are invisible in agent traces that start at your app server.
cards.apply: Send W3C traceparent headers from your agent runtime through the proxy and enable OpenTelemetry tracing there so edge spans land in the same trace as tool and model calls.
cards.result: A slow tool call can be attributed to the edge, origin, or model in one trace view.

evidence.note: Editorial inference from Cloudflare's open-beta Traces announcement.
